questions.question: Which principle does a stack follow?
questions.explanation: The most recently pushed element is popped first.

questions.question: Which principle does a queue follow?
options: Last In, Last Out only for priorities
questions.explanation: Elements are removed in the order they were added.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an array element by index?
questions.explanation: Contiguous storage allows direct address calculation.

questions.question: A node in a singly linked list typically stores:
options: Data and references to all other nodes
Data and a reference to the next node
questions.explanation: Each node holds its value and a pointer to its successor.

questions.question: In a tree, what is a node with no children called?
questions.explanation: Leaves are nodes without children.

questions.question: Push 1, 2, 3 onto an empty stack, then pop once. Which value is removed?
questions.explanation: The last pushed value, 3, is on top.

questions.question: Which data structure maps keys to values using a hash function?
questions.explanation: A hash table computes a bucket index from each key.

questions.question: Which data structure is used to implement breadth-first search?
questions.explanation: BFS processes vertices in the order they are discovered, using a FIFO queue.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of inserting at the head of a singly linked list?
questions.explanation: Only the new node's next pointer and the head pointer change.

questions.question: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits keys in ascending order?
questions.explanation: In-order visits left subtree, node, then right subtree.

questions.question: For a hash table with chaining, what are the average and worst-case lookup times?
options: Average O(log n), worst O(log n)
questions.explanation: With a good hash, chains stay short; if all keys collide, lookup scans n items.

questions.question: In a binary min-heap with n elements, where is the minimum and what does extract-min cost (worst case)?
options: At the last index; O(log n)
questions.explanation: The root holds the minimum; removing it requires sifting down along the height.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height h (a single root has height 0)?
questions.explanation: A perfect binary tree has 1 + 2 + ... + 2^h = 2^(h+1) - 1 nodes.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of a circular (ring buffer) queue over a simple array queue?
options: It allows access to any element in O(1) by key
It reuses slots freed by dequeues without shifting elements
It never needs a fixed capacity
questions.explanation: Wrapping indices modulo capacity lets freed front slots be reused.

questions.question: Which data structure supports insertion and deletion at both ends?
questions.explanation: A double-ended queue allows operations at the front and back.

questions.question: What is the space complexity of an adjacency matrix for a graph with V vertices and E edges?
questions.explanation: The matrix has V x V entries regardless of edge count.

questions.question: What is the worst-case search time in an unbalanced binary search tree with n nodes?
questions.explanation: Inserting sorted keys degenerates the tree into a linked-list-like chain.

questions.question: Which property does an AVL tree maintain at every node?
options: All leaves are at the same depth
Every node is red or black
Left child is always larger than the node
Subtree heights differ by at most 1
questions.explanation: The balance factor in {-1, 0, 1} keeps height O(log n).

questions.question: What is the amortized time of append in a dynamic array that doubles its capacity when full?
questions.explanation: Occasional O(n) copies are spread over many cheap appends.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time to build a binary heap from n unsorted elements using bottom-up heapify?
questions.explanation: Most nodes are near the leaves and sift down only a short distance, summing to O(n).

questions.question: In a trie, what is the worst-case time to search for a word of length L?
options: O(n), where n is the number of stored words
questions.explanation: Search follows one edge per character, independent of how many words are stored.

questions.question: With union by rank and path compression, what is the amortized cost per Union-Find operation?
questions.explanation: The combination yields nearly constant amortized time, bounded by the inverse Ackermann function.
